headlines.title: 2 people hurt after shooting on Highway 101 in San Carlos
headlines.description: Two people were injured following a shooting on Highway 101 in San Carlos Sunday afternoon, according to the California Highway Patrol. CHP said they received reports of two minor injuries from a shooting on northbound Highway 101, south of Ralston, at around 5 p.m.; one person was grazed by a bullet, while another person suffered an injury to their back. Authorities said northbound Highway 101 at Holly Street was closed as officers investigate the incident. Hours later, CHP announced all lanes reopened. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: Man arrested after shootout near Manzanita Park in Oakland
headlines.description: A man was arrested after allegedly threatening to kill a woman and shooting at officers near Manzanita Park in Oakland on Sunday, police said. The police department said they received multiple 911 calls at 10:30 a.m. about a man threatening to kill a woman at Manzanita Park. Police arrived at the scene, and the suspect immediately began shooting at the officers, authorities said. Officials said the officers returned fired and the suspect fled to the neighborhood. Authorities added the woman was rescued and taken to a safe place. Oakland PD set up a command center inside the perimeter, which encompassed the Manzanita Park neighborhood. Authorities said the suspect hid at an abandoned home in the 2600 block of 22nd Avenue. Just before 3 p.m., the suspect lit items on fire, threw them at officers and set the home ablaze. “During that process he started throwing flammable cans, that he lit on fire, at police officers, and he lit the building that he was in on fire. The officers had to emergency deploy smoke, to get him to exit the building, at which point our canine-tactical team took him into custody,” Oakland Police Department Chief James Beere said. Police said the suspect exited the house and fought officers as they tried to take him into custody. The suspect was taken to an Oakland hospital for injuries sustained in the arrest, according to the police department. Beere said investigators believe the gunman knew the woman rescued by officers.. This is a developing story. Details may change as more information becomes available. Stay tuned for updates.

headlines.title: San Francisco police investigate double stabbing
headlines.description: Two people were stabbed in San Francisco Sunday afternoon, according to police. Investigators say this happened near O’Farrell Street, not too far from the Powell BART station, around 3 p.m. Police say both victims walked into a hospital emergency room, which prompted them to respond to the stabbing location. Both are expected to be okay. So far, police have not made any arrests.

headlines.title: Nepali Americans in the Bay Area continue fundraising for flood relief efforts
headlines.description: Many Bay Area residents have loved ones who were impacted by the devastating flooding this week at the border between Nepal and China’s Tibet region. In Nepal, the country’s disaster agency reports that 781 people have died and more than 2,500 people remain missing. China has reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing in the Tibet region. Members of the Bay Area Nepalese community and local supporters gathered Sunday for an emergency relief fundraiser and candlelight vigil in Berkeley. Quite a few of the people in attendance knew people who had been reported as dead or missing in the flooding. The event was hosted by the Taste of the Himalayas restaurant on Shattuck Avenue. Organizers said the gathering aims to honor those affected, raise vital funds for relief efforts, and demonstrate solidarity with the Nepalese community. Ram Paudel, with the Taste of the Himalayas restaurant, posted a sign outside his business with links directing people to donate to relief efforts organized by the government in Nepal. Paudel explained that he grew up in the Nuwakot district of Nepal, one of the areas impacted by the flooding. He noted he has a cousin who was caught up in the flood waters. “We don’t know, we are hoping he might be back, but we are still praying,” he said of his cousin. Paudel said he hosted the event to encourage people in the Bay Area to contribute in “any way they can.” Also at the vigil was one woman who explained, with translation help from her friend, that her daughter, husband, brother, and sister-in-law had all been swept away in the flooding in the Nuwakot district. “It’s not only her family lost, her village, house, she doesn’t have anything now,” explained the woman’s friend. Many with ties to the Bay Area have been impacted by this flooding. Several news outlets, including CNN, have interviewed a couple from the Bay Area who said they were on a pilgrimage when the flood waters hit, but incredibly, made it out alive. “I saw something coming, really brown up there, like 60 to 70 feet, something coming brown our way,” recalled Anjana Raja in the interview with CNN. A Milpitas man who was on a pilgrimage is also reported to be among those missing after the flooding. At the Berkeley gathering on Sunday, Paudel was on video chat with several people in Nepal, including Nepalese Minister of Information and Communication Bikram Timilsina. While on video chat, Timilsina spoke with NBC Bay Area News, explaining that it has been difficult to reach the flooded areas by land, so relief efforts require helicopters to access them. Timilsina described villages being swept away in the flood waters and efforts ramping up to retrieve more bodies from the impacted zones. Uttam Karki, a Nepali American who was at the event, explained that his family and friends in Nepal believe the scale of loss from this disaster is even greater than the numbers show presently. He’s hoping other Americans learn about what is happening in the aftermath of this flood and offer up financial support if they are able. “That’s what I would like to ask everyone in the American community, you don’t have to be Nepalese to help,” he said.
headlines.source: NBC Bay Area staff and Alyssa Goard

headlines.title: Firefighters knock down 1-acre brush fire in Southeast San Jose
headlines.description: Firefighters quickly knocked down a 1-acre brush fire Sunday morning in the hills of southeast San Jose. Crews from Cal Fire and the San Jose Fire Department responded just before 7 a.m. to reports of a vegetation fire near Metcalf Road. Upon arrival, firefighters encountered a 1-acre blaze sending a large plume of smoke into the air that was visible across parts of South San Jose. Fire crews made rapid progress, stopping the spread and knocking down the fire in about 15 minutes. No injuries were reported. Fire officials said a car fire was what sparked the fire.

headlines.title: Canoers found dead after boating trip in Tomales Bay
headlines.description: Two canoers were found dead Sunday after an overnight boating trip in Tomales Bay. First responders say the men took off for a night “luminescence” trip around midnight. Multiple agencies deployed searchers from the water, ground and air. The body of one man was found in the ocean, just outside the mouth of Tomales Bay. The second man was found on shore, just north of Hog Island in the Bay. Both were wearing life jackets. Emergency responders say this area is notoriously dangerous. Investigators say it’s not clear yet how the two ended up in the water.

headlines.title: Plaskett Fire prompts new evacuations, more Timber Fire evacuations possible
headlines.description: New evacuation orders and evacuation warnings were issued on Saturday due to the Plaskett Fire burning in Monterey County, authorities said. This comes as fire crews also battle the Timber Fire, further north in Monterey County, where officials warned some Carmel Valley residents that more evacuation orders could be issued later this week. According to Cal Fire, the Plaskett Fire was reported on Wednesday, a few weeks after the Timber Fire erupted on Aug. 8. Both wildfires are burning along the Big Sur coast, with the Plaskett Fire burning 8,241 acres with 0% containment and the Timber Fire burning 24,601 acres and 21% containment as of Saturday afternoon. On Saturday, at around 3 p.m., the United States Army Garrison – Fort Hunger Ligget issued an evacuation order for zone MRY-G012-A and an evacuation warning for the zones MRY-G011-A and MRY-G012-B. Hours earlier, the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office issued an evacuation order for the zone MRY-F037 and an evacuation warning for the zones RY-F038 and MRY-F039. At least one structure was destroyed in the Plaskett Fire. For more information, visit the county’s emergency alerts website. As of Saturday evening, CAL FIRE said that steep terrain and lots of fuel for the fire “continue to create significant challenges for suppression efforts” on the Timber Fire, adding that fire spread is expected toward the Lucia Range, South Fork Trail and the Black Cone Trail. Big Sur resident Jessica Swan said she can see the Timber Fire from where she lives, and the flames can look intimidating, especially when “the winds pick up, and you see those big trees catch on fire.” “We are talking about 200-foot flames, it looks like,” she noted. Swan lives in one of the areas that is under a shelter-in-place order due to the fire. “I’m up here for maybe a week, it could keep going,” she noted. “You know everyone’s prepared with food and water if you were to go down to the highway, it’s just police and fire trucks.” Highway 1 is closed off near Swan in Big Sur as well as further south near the Plaskett Fire. At a Town Meeting Saturday at Cachagua Community Park, county officials warned residents that this week dry conditions with low humidity are expected, and if the Timber Fire continues progressing, more evacuation orders may need to be issued in the Carmel Valley. At that meeting, in reference to comments from Chief Deputy Eric Bixler with the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office, Monterey County Supervisor Kate Daniels told attendees, ” I think everyone should take that as your warning and start preparing now and expect that sometime this week you will get an evacuation order.” While law enforcement officials said they can’t predict the odds of having to issue more evacuation orders, they advised community members to be prepared in the event that happens. Dylan Flynn, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, noted, “as the fire burns further into the wilderness, it’s drier, and we also get stronger winds the higher we go up in elevation.” “So as we start going from the two- and 3-thousand-foot mountains we had a few weeks ago on the Timber Fire, to these higher elevations, 4-5 thousand-foot peaks, the winds are gonna be stronger,” Flynn continued, noting that the dry weather and low humidity can dry out some of the vegetation, which in turn can fuel the fire. Firefighters expect to be at work on these fires for a while to get them contained. They are asking the public to keep the roadways clear near the fires and to drive with caution. Additionally, fire officials are urging the public to have ‘go-bags’ and neccessary supplies like medications ready just in case more evacuations are ordered. “We don’t want people to have a false sense of security that just because it’s cooler that things are gonna be potentially less active, and we really want to advocate for people to be prepared,” said Josh Silveira, a Public Information Officer for CAL FIRE. Silveira said that if the Timber Fire keeps pushing northeast, it’s possible evacuation warnings or orders could be issued for the communities of Tassajara and Cachagua. He noted that around Big Sur, there is “very limited access into the wilderness” and that in order to do firefighting work on the steep terrain, firefighters are re-opening a series of historic fire breaks. For those who live outside of the area, Silveira encourages them to stay away from the fire zone and to visit other areas of Monterey County instead. Evacuation shelters have been designated for the Timber and Plaskett Fires at Carmel Mission Inn Conference Room, 3665 Rio Road in Carmel, and at Cambria Veterans Memorial Building in Cambria.

headlines.title: 3 Bay Area residents among 4 killed in remote Alaska plane crash
headlines.description: Three Bay Area residents were among four people killed when a small plane crashed in a slough near the remote Alaska community of Seldovia on Aug. 26. Alaska authorities identified the victims as Ronald Schmidt, 65, and Lance Schmidt, 20, both of San Jose, along with Daniel Simons, 82, of Los Gatos. The pilot, Eric Middlebrook, 68, of Anchorage, was also killed. The aircraft, a Piper PA-24, was traveling from Anchorage to Seldovia when it went down and sank in shallow water in the Seldovia Slough. Recovery efforts were initially delayed until the tide receded, which allowed emergency crews to safely reach the submerged wreckage. The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the cause of the crash.

headlines.title: San Jose police officer injured in shootout released from hospital
headlines.description: SJPD confirmed Saturday the officer injured during a shootout at a home on Tuesday was released from the hospital. The shootout happened in a home near Tamien Park. Police first spotted a Stolen Chevy Tahoe associated with two recent armed robberies. After a short chase the suspect, identified as Anthony Chavez, crashed into multiple cars before running into a home while a family was inside. Police got the family out and found Chavez hiding in a bathroom. That’s when they say Chavez immediately started shooting at officers, injuring Sergeant Matt Walsh. Walsh and another officer returned fire, ultimately killing Chavez. San Jose Aug 26 San Jose Aug 27 San Jose Aug 25 San Jose police officer injured, suspect killed following shootout

headlines.title: Silicon Valley Pride kicks off 51st annual festival in Downtown San Jose
headlines.description: Thousands gathered in downtown San Jose on Saturday night as Silicon Valley Pride kicked off its 51st annual celebration along Market Street with music, dancing and community gathering. The festival, held under the theme “Flourish and Bloom,” served as a prelude to Sunday’s grand parade. Attendees engaged in a range of festivities, including drag performances, food vendors and local artisan shops. For many in attendance, the event represented a vital space for acceptance, visibility, and mutual support amid challenging times. “We’re a part of everybody. We’re no different than everybody else, and I think that’s important,” said Tommy Soeung of San Francisco. Harry Apodaca of Redwood Shores echoed that sentiment, emphasizing the significance of community celebration. “Because it’s the opposite of despair,” Apodaca said. “Trans joy, queer joy is something we can do to resist.” While LGBTQ+ pride events in nearby San Francisco often command the national spotlight, the festival gave the South Bay community its own dedicated stage to showcase creativity and unity. “I’m obviously gay, and I am here to support Pride,” said Daniel Hernandez of San Jose. Rabi Singh, also of San Jose, noted that local representation remains essential for the community’s presence. “When it comes down to it, it’s about visibility,” Singh said. “It’s important, showing people here that we are present and celebrated and should be appreciated.” The celebrations continue Sunday morning with the Silicon Valley Pride Parade on Market Street, scheduled to begin at 10:30 a.m.

headlines.title: San Francisco authorities focus on safety at PokémonXP
headlines.description: San Francisco is hosting one of the biggest weekends in the Pokémon franchise’s history. With some collectibles worth thousands of dollars, there’s another battle happening behind the scenes: keeping it all safe. Thousands of fans, competitors and collectors from around the world gathered at the Pokémon XP and the World Championships in San Francisco. For many of the fans, the events also mean a lot of shopping. “My total at Pokémon Center for San Francisco was $1,119,” Washington resident Austin Reno said. “I brought about $8,000 of cards to trade and sell.” That’s why safety is serious business this weekend in San Francisco. San Francisco Aug 28 San Francisco Giants Aug 27 San Francisco Aug 27 Some of the most coveted cards at Aloha Card Shop’s booth can fetch five, even six figures; with big money, comes bigger risks. “Especially nowadays with all the money coming into the hobby, there’s a lot of ne’er-do-wells looking for a quick buck, so you really have to be vigilant. We’ve had people steal from us in the past because there’s so much going on and it’s easy to let something slip,” Aloha Card Shop Co-Owner Reece Felix said. Ali Reid has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Attempted murder suspect arrested in East Palo Alto
headlines.description: On Saturday, several law enforcement agencies teamed up to arrest an attempted murder suspect in East Palo Alto. Authorities say the suspect led officers on a chase that ended in the Bay, at the Ravenswood Preserve. This prompted a response from East Palo Alto police, San Mateo County deputies, a CHP chopper, and an airboat crew from the Menlo Park Fire District. Once brought out of the water, the suspect was treated by paramedics. Police say the man was wanted for a shooting back in April.
